title: Introduce Theme Mechanism
description:
Introduce a theme mechanism. The default theme is the semio theme. In os and playgrounds add a theme tab to settings side panel where premade themes can be selected, and customized. Add save and load mechanism. All tokens are editable in tree etc.

Approach (see full plan in ticket folder / conversation): rename the existing light/dark palette dimension from "theme" to "appearance" (freeing "theme" for this new concept); build a UiTheme model covering colors, spacing, fontStacks, canvasFonts, strokes, radii, opacities, metrics, and appearances (light/dark palette groups); extend runtime merge bridges beyond colors to all tokens; add a Theme settings tab (select premades semio+mono, edit every token in a tree, save/load custom themes via localStorage + .theme.json export/import) in the shared os-shell settings panel (covers os and playgrounds/studio since they share the same shell).
summary:
Fixed: "mono" premade theme was not selectable in the Theme tab. Root cause was a real bug, not a stale dev server as I'd suspected earlier — `builtinUiThemes()` guarded its `import.meta.glob(...)` call with `typeof import.meta.glob === "function"`, but that check is always false at runtime in every environment (including real Vite browser bundles): Vite's glob plugin only rewrites the literal `import.meta.glob(...)` call expression at build time, it never polyfills `import.meta.glob` as an actual runtime property, so a bare `typeof` probe of it is always `undefined`/false. Confirmed via direct testing on a clean, self-started dev server: Vite correctly hoisted the static import for mono.theme.json (network request fired, JSON parsed fine, parseUiTheme succeeded standalone) — but the `if` guard around the loop that pushes it into the themes array was always skipped, so `builtinUiThemes()` silently returned only semio.

Fixed by calling `import.meta.glob(...)` directly inside a try/catch instead of probing for it first — Vite still statically transforms the call regardless of try/catch wrapping, so the browser path works correctly; outside Vite (bun scripts, tests) the call throws (import.meta.glob is genuinely undefined there) and is caught, falling back to semio-only as before. Also tightened the corresponding inline vitest test, which previously silently skipped its assertion when mono wasn't found instead of failing — that's exactly why this shipped unnoticed — and added an explicit "builtinUiThemes discovers the mono premade" test.

Verified end-to-end on a fresh, self-started Vite dev server (not the shared one from another session): mono now appears in the theme picker, selecting it correctly recolors the whole UI chrome to grayscale, and computed --color-primary / data-ui-theme reflect the switch.

Also found the identical broken guard pattern in cad/runtime/js/index.ts's shippedModelDefinitionAssets() (I had copied this pattern from there originally) — likely means CAD model-definition assets never load in the real app either. Did not fix it myself (different subsystem, unverified impact) — flagged it as a separate follow-up task instead.
